answer: An attacker planning 1,000 fake identities faces admission auctions. Each epoch, 100 identity slots go to the highest bidders. The floor price is 50 units. Bidders push each other up. A dawn of new demand raises prices fast. A copper floor keeps honest agents in: verified workers bid from earned rewards, not fresh capital. To win 1,000 slots, it must outbid honest agents 10 epochs running. At 120 units per slot, 1,000 identities cost 120,000 units. Caught fakes lose the slot and the bid; a signal of scarcity is public.
